title.narrative: IUCN: PAGE (Partenariat pour la Gouvernance Environmentale)
IUCN: PAGE (Partnership for Env Govern West Africa)

description.narrative: Poverty reduction and environmental management IUCN Relevance Assessment: The development intervention’s objectives and intended results are in line with the strategy objectives, or equivalent, and relevant policy adopted by the Swedish Government and Sida’s operational plan. Results analysis and effectiveness: The development intervention has objectives that enable monitoring and results reporting, the potential to achieve its objectives and a budget that is reasonable in relation to the objectives and expected results. Organisational capacity: internal control: The cooperation partner/partners has the potential to deliver outputs in an efficient manner and sufficient capacity to maintain an adequate level of internal control including capacity to manage for results. Sustainability and ownership: The development intervention has the potential to achieve sustainability in its objectives. Alignment and Harmonisation: Swedish funding is aligned to the partner/partners’s regular systems and any deviations have been motivated. A programme Based Approach and harmonised financing have been sought after. Sida's assessment of how the principles of alignment and harmonisation have been considered in the Swedish contribution has been documented.

Relevansbedömning: Mål och resultat för utvecklingsinsatsen bidrar till att uppnå av regeringen beslutade strategimål eller motsvarande samt är förenliga med övriga av regeringen beslutade styrande dokument för biståndet och Sidas verksamhetsplan. Resultatanalys och måluppfyllelse: Utvecklingsinsatsen har mål som möjliggör uppföljning och rapportering av resultat, har förutsättningar att uppnå sina mål och en rimlig budget i förhållande till mål och förväntade resultat. Organisationskapacitet: intern styrning och kontroll: Samarbetspart har förutsättningar att leverera prestationer (”output”) på ett effektivt sätt och en tillräcklig intern styrning och kontroll inklusive förutsättningar att styra insatsen mot överenskomna mål. Hållbarhet och ägarskap: Utvecklingsinsatsen har förutsättningar att uppnå långsiktig uthållighet i de effekter som utvecklingsinsatsen ska leda till. Anpassning och harmonisering: Finansieringen har anpassats till samarbetspartens/parternas system och eventuella avsteg har motiverats. En programansats och samordnad finansiering har eftersträvats. Sidas bedömning av hur principerna för anpassning och harmonisering har beaktats i den svenska insatsen har dokumenterats.

sector.narrative: Water sector policy and administrative management

description.narrative:
The final evaluation concludes that the PAGE program has been highly relevant (86%), very effective both in terms of implementation according to plan (77% 6 months ahead of final closure) and in reducing the severity of the problems addressed (86%), reasonably cost efficient and able to handle external risk, with most results achieved needing further follow-up to ensure sustainability, and an overall impact mostly at the level of environmental governance where PAGE has contributed to lay the foundations for reinforced governance of water resources, rather than significantly improving the conditions of the ecosystems in question. Finally, the evaluation report also notes a number of reasons why the type of partnerships offered by IUCN with subregional actors is appreciated by the latter (flexibility, visibility, 'branding' and institutional learning) while also noting that reporting from these partners is weak on youth and gender analysis.
Conclusions of the Evaluation in relation to the Specific Objectives (SOs) and examples of results achieved: SO1: To contribute to the implementation of Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) in the Volta, Niger, Senegal and Mono Basins: The level of achievement of SO1 outcomes is 74% (as per the methodology of the final evaluation). Of the four sub-results linked to SO1, one is not achieved due to an overly optimistic assessment of the issues related to the legal and institutional reform efforts prior to the establishment of water agencies. Examples of results achieved under this objective include a large number of representatives from civil society and local government (160) have been trained in understanding the ECOWAS water policy framework, several statutory consultation mechanisms have been operationalized, the Niger river basin agency's data processing centre (observatory) has become functional (and the one for the Volta river basin agency considerably improved) and several legal instruments in the area of water management have been developed or improved.
SO2: To contribute to the mainstreaming of the environmental dimension in the management of the Volta, Niger, Senegal and Mono Basins; The average level of achievement of SO2 outcomes is 65%. It is largely affected by the delayed availability of the decision support tool to be developed by IUCN to help estimate environmental costs, benefits and risks by Niger Basin Authority and the Volta Basin Authority in their respective basins. Examples of results achieved under this objective include a decision support tool for the water agencies / river basin organisations - however delayed and therefore the impact of this tool during the program period was limited- but also awareness raising campaigns on the importance of the preservation of the environment targeted to parliamentarians as well as the general public via radio programs.
SO3: To contribute to the sustainable management of the goods and services derived from the ecosystems in the Niger, Volta, Senegal and Mono Basins; The level of achievement of SO3 outcomes is 91% compared to the end-June 2018 target. It shows a very good performance of knowledge acquisition and awareness-raising activities, albeit with a limited number of people at policy/decision making level. In view of the high rate of staff mobility in general in the water agency and other key institutions, the number of people trained - while not insignificant - could jeopardise the long-term sustainability of results under this objective. Examples of results achieved under this objective include a number of publications (14) on the economic value of specific ecosystems and training of institutional actors (39) in methods to arrive at such estimates, as well as training and support to local communities in sustainable management of natural resources and to small local, rural enterprises applying such technologies.
SO4: To contribute to the mainstreaming of climate change in national and local planning in the Niger, Volta, Senegal and Mono Basins; With an implementation level of 56% (in June 2018), the achievements under OS4 is at an average level compared to the target (which might have been to ambitious), mainly because of the limited number of local development plans (LDP) revised to integrate the environment and climate change dimensions, which in turn is due to the lengthy revision process given its participatory and didactic nature vis-à-vis the communities involved. The proposed methodology likely have to be simplified. Examples of results achieved under this objective include 11 local development plans (out of a planned 14) by the end of PAGE (Dec 2018) and one new country adopting a methodological tool for integrating climate and environment into the LDPs.
SO5: To contribute to the restoration of degraded ecosystems in the Niger, Volta, Senegal and Mono Basins; The level of achievement of SO5 results is 100%, i.e. full realization, both in terms of the number of good practices acquired by communities (7), and in terms of management plans (11) developed and implemented for the management of gallery forests and source heads. Examples of results achieved under this objective include 8 pilot sites selected in a participatory manner in which PAGE has supported the restoration of ecosystems in partnership with NGOs and research institutions and based on the ownership and leadership of the communities themselves which also included the formulation of local agreements on the continued protection and management of the restored ecosystems.
Taken together, the results under the various SOs are assessed to contribute to an overall improved governance of natural and in particular water resources in that it reinforces and en empowers the various actors concerned in their different roles and mandates where the intergovernmental organisations (ECOWAS, WAEMU, CILSS) develop and monitor policy, the river basin organisations operationalize and ensure implementation of the policy frameworks, individual member states implements in close cooperation with local governments, civil society and local communities ensures local needs and perspectives are taken into account, research organisations support in knowledge production, media in dissemination and awareness raising and international partners in financing. Establishing these partnerships and activating these dynamics should also be seen as an important outcome under the PAGE program.
